notes: Prompts and answer choices are transcribed verbatim from Find_Your_Class_Pilot_Blueprint_v1.md section 8 (Q1-Q12). criteriaClarified and each answer's mutation direction are a first structural mapping onto assets/find-your-class/criteria.json -- the blueprint specifies player-facing wording and intent, not exact numeric mutation payloads, so mutations here are qualitative (criterionId + direction/desiredPosition/importanceHint) pending Codex's numeric calibration. Section 9's discriminator list (Fighter vs Magus, Sorcerer vs Druid, etc.) is separate adaptive-selection logic, not part of this static template file.

allowNotRelevant is true for every question per the blueprint's own answer lists, which each include a literal 'Not relevant' option except Q10 (campaign levels, which has no Not relevant option in the blueprint).

Contract, fixed after Codex's review of commit 8c5efdd: (1) a capability-kind criterion (criteria.json kind:"capability") is only ever mutated with importanceHint/importance + notRelevant, never desiredPosition -- desiredPosition is exclusively for directional-kind criteria, and loader.js's checkKindMatch() now rejects the wrong field for a criterion's kind. (2) 'Not relevant' on a question clarifying more than one criterion must clear every criterion listed in that question's criteriaClarified, not just the first one. (3) every answer's mutations array is either non-empty or the answer carries nonScoring:true -- an empty array with no flag is always a bug, not an intentional no-op (Q1/Q2's 'no strong lean' answers, Q6's UI-mode toggle, Q10's 'I do not know', and Q12's three navigation-only options are the only nonScoring:true cases).

questions.prompt: What should make your character feel powerful?

answers.label: Having magic for almost every problem.
I am open to any of these.

questions.prompt: Where do you want to spend most fights?

answers.label: Moving between close and medium range.
I want to switch depending on the encounter.

questions.prompt: How do you feel about choosing spells or abilities before the adventuring day begins?

answers.label: I enjoy preparing the right tools.

questions.prompt: What kind of combat turns sound enjoyable?

answers.label: A reliable plan I can execute quickly.
A few strong choices without too much bookkeeping.
Many tactical choices and interacting abilities.

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy controlling another creature?

answers.label: No; I want to manage only my own character.
A simple familiar or occasional summon is fine.
I want a meaningful animal companion or similar partner.

questions.prompt: What would you most like to contribute outside combat?

answers.label: Choose several.
notes: UI-mode toggle: switches this question into multi-select. multiSelect:true already allows picking several of the checkbox answers directly; this option carries no preference of its own.

questions.prompt: When combat starts, what sounds most satisfying?

answers.label: Controlling where enemies can move or act.
Adapting to whatever the fight needs.

questions.prompt: How much danger do you want your character to withstand directly?
notes: personal-durability and protect-allies are both kind:"capability" -- every answer below uses importanceHint, never desiredPosition (fixed after Codex's review: the pre-review version wrongly wrote desiredPosition against personal-durability, a capability criterion).

answers.label: I am comfortable relying on positioning and avoiding attacks.
I want reasonable protection if enemies reach me.
I want to be difficult to bring down.
I want to stand between enemies and my allies.

questions.prompt: Would you rather perfect one plan or keep many answers available?

answers.label: Have a main plan plus alternatives.

questions.prompt: When does this character need to feel complete?
notes: Writes campaignContext.startingLevel/expectedEndLevel, not a scored criterion -- see Find_Your_Class_Product_Architecture_v1.md section 10.6.

answers.label: I am comfortable waiting until levels 6-10.

questions.prompt: How do you like to spend limited power?

answers.label: I prefer abilities I can rely on all day.
I like a steady baseline with a few stronger moments.
I enjoy deciding when to unleash powerful limited resources.

questions.prompt: Which fantasy is closest, even if none is exact?
notes: Blueprint 8/Q12: present only 4-6 fantasy cards selected from the concept and current shortlist, plus the three fixed options below. Card population is dynamic (drawn from vocabularies.json fantasyTags filtered by the current shortlist), not a fixed answer list -- only the trailing fixed options are static, and none of the three carries a mutation of its own (they navigate: show more cards / dismiss / skip the question).
